title: Is Render Free? Free Tier Limits, Sleep, and the 30-Day DB (2026)
description: Is Render free? Yes â genuinely, permanently, no card: free web services, a free Postgres, free static sites, on a $0 Hobby workspace as of 2026. It is also engineered so that a business cannot live on it. Free services sleep after 15 idle minutes and take a minute to wake. A workspace gets 750 free hours a month. The free database deletes itself 30 days after you create it. And while your app is asleep, Render answers `/robots.txt` with disallow all. Free Render is a sandbox with the walls painted to look like a house. ... Render's free tier is one of the few in hosting that doesn't hide a clause. Vercel's Hobby plan is free until you charge a customer, because the license says non-commercial. Railway's "free" is a one-time $5 credit. Render's is different: no commercial restriction, no trial clock on the compute itself, no card. What Render does instead is make the free tier behave like a demo. Sleep after 15 minutes. One minute to wake. A database with a 30-day fuse. A robots.txt that tells search engines to go away whenever nobody's visiting. As of September 2026, every one of those is documented on render.com, and every one of them is the reason a real product moves to the $7 instance within a month. The rest of this post is the detail, with the numbers. ... The free Postgres is where the real fuse is. Per render.com/docs/free as of 2026: only one free Postgres per workspace, 1 GB of storage, no backups of any kind, no connection pooling, and it expires 30 days after creation. Expired means inaccessible. After a further 14-day grace period, Render deletes the database and everything in it. You get emails as both deadlines approach. The fix is to upgrade the database to any paid compute plan, and the smallest is $6 a month for 256 MB. That is the actual price of Render's free tier for anything with users: $6, on day 30. The free Key Value instance has a version of the same problem â in-memory only, so every restart empties it, and Render reserves the right to restart free instances at any time. ... - Render: free, no commercial clause, but sleeps in 15 minutes, caps at 750 hours, and expires its database in 30 days. Free for hobbies by design. - Vercel ... and a million function calls ... until the Stripe button. ... Yes. As of 2026, Render's Hobby workspace plan is $0 a month and you can run web services, one Postgres database, one Key Value instance, and unlimited static sites on free compute with no time limit and no card. The limits are behavioral rather than a license: free web services spin down after 15 minutes without traffic and take about a minute to wake, a workspace gets 750 free instance hours a month, and the free Postgres expires 30 days after you create it. Render's own docs say not to use free instances for production. ... Per render.com/docs/free and render.com/pricing as of 2026: free web services run on 512 MB of RAM and a fractional CPU, sleep after 15 idle minutes, share 750 free instance hours per workspace per month, and cannot scale past one instance, attach a persistent disk, open a shell, run one-off jobs, or send outbound mail on ports 25, 465, or 587. The free Postgres is limited to one per workspace, 1 GB of storage, no backups, and a 30-day lifetime with a 14-day grace period before deletion. The Hobby workspace itself includes 5 GB of outbound bandwidth, 500 build minutes, 2 custom domains, and 7 days of logs. ... Yes. A free Render Postgres database expires 30 days after creation. Once expired it is inaccessible unless you upgrade it to a paid compute plan, and after a further 14-day grace period Render deletes the database and all of its data. Render emails you as the expiry and the end of the grace period approach, and free databases have no backups of any kind, so if the data matters, the $6 a month paid tier is the actual price of the free tier. ... They are three different bargains. Render is free with no commercial-use restriction but sleeps after 15 minutes and expires its database after 30 days. Vercel's Hobby plan never sleeps and is far more generous on usage, but it is restricted to personal, non-commercial use, so the first paying customer ends it. Railway has no permanent free tier at all, just a one-time $5 trial credit, and then $5 a month with $5 of usage included and no sleeping or commercial clause. For a hobby project, Render or Vercel; for anything a customer will hit, Railway's $5 or Render's $7 paid instance.
